label: Scissor Tail Editions
description: Six long pieces that push steel-string American Primitive playing toward drone: slide lines bend like raga figures on 'Corvid Tactics', and side two adds violin and electronic haze under the guitar on 'The Deer and the Snake'. The electrified closer hints at the pedal-steel ambient records he made next. For listeners who like William Tyler or Jack Rose but want the pieces to drift further out.
lineage: Sits in the Fahey and Basho line as carried on by the 2010s Scissor Tail and VDSQ circle; its drones point toward the ambient-country crossover of Chuck Johnson's own later pedal-steel work.

label: Friends House Records
description: A ten-song record where big hooks and feedback crash into banjo, mandolin, accordion and toy instruments, with shouted, harmonized vocals and loose studio chatter left in. It swings hard between hushed folk moments and punk blowouts, which puts it on the emo-twang side of the map. For listeners who like their folk-punk messy and their emo with a string band in the room.
lineage: Folk-punk-leaning emo that sounds indebted to Titus Andronicus's rowdier moments and the Pinegrove-era emo-twang crossover; its acoustic instruments tie it to the DIY folk revival around the Core.
borderline_note: Field-guide 'Unplaced (2026)' artist; placed in C9 by sound (emo/folk-punk with banjo and mandolin).
